cohort: The study included 193 women (40 primiparas and 153 multiparas), all at least 40 years old at conception and delivering after 22 completed weeks of gestation, who gave birth between 2009-2014 at a Medical University in Warsaw.
finding: Delayed childbearing of a first child (primiparity in women over 40) is associated with an increased risk of perinatal complications such as oligohydramnios, pregnancy-induced hypertension, operative delivery, unsuccessful labor inductions, and fibroids, compared to multiparous women of similar age.
mod_finding: Primiparas had a significantly greater risk of operative delivery (RR=1.83) and unsuccessful labor inductions (RR=3.60).
birth_weight: N/A (no relation between parity and birth weight observed, specific weights not mentioned)
